message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta.  
Here’s how:

| Step | What to do | Where to go / Who to contact |
|------|------------|------------------------------|
| 1 | **Check the city’s noise ordinance** – Atlanta’s ordinance defines what constitutes “excessive noise” and the hours during which it is prohibited. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety> |
| 2 | **File a complaint online** – Use the City’s 311 portal to submit a noise complaint. You’ll need to provide the location, time, and description of the noise. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| 3 | **Call the Atlanta Police Department** – If the noise is urgent or you prefer to speak directly, call 911 for emergencies or 404‑656‑4000 for non‑emergencies. | Atlanta Police Department – 404‑656‑4000 |
| 4 | **Contact the City’s Office of Noise Control** – For ongoing or repeated complaints, you can reach out to the Office of Noise Control. | Email: noisecontrol@atlantaga.gov |
| 5 | **Follow up** – After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any follow‑up questions or status checks. | |

**Quick Tips**

* **Timing matters** – Noise complaints are most effective when filed during the hours the ordinance prohibits excessive noise (typically 10 p.m.–6 a.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m.–6 a.m. on weekends).
* **Document evidence** – If possible, record the noise or note the exact times and dates. This helps the authorities assess the situation.
* **Know your rights** – The city’s noise ordinance protects residents from disturbances that interfere with sleep, health, or safety.

If you’re unsure whether your situation qualifies as a noise violation, you can also call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line for guidance.
